proposed_comments.title: Enforce caller isolation beyond executable identity
proposed_comments.body:
### Enforce caller isolation beyond executable identity

**Severity:** `critical`

The service authorizes opaque `PutBlob` requests from the owning SID by checking the client image basename, Microsoft signature, and exact file version. A same-user process can still inject into an already-running accepted PowerToys process and issue arbitrary writes through that identity, so the new boundary does not provide tamper resistance against the stated same-user attacker. Please put write authority behind an OS-enforced token/capability boundary that prevents such injection, or replace opaque blob writes with constrained service-side operations and validation; include a negative end-to-end test showing that untrusted same-user code cannot mutate protected state through an authorized process.

proposed_comments.title: Add a service-boundary security regression suite
proposed_comments.body:
### Add a service-boundary security regression suite

**Severity:** `high`

The current native tests cover path helpers, predictable-pipe squatting, SID syntax, and namespace traversal, but they do not provision the packaged Release service or exercise its trust and lifecycle boundary. Signer/version/basename/SID rejection, pipe ACLs and stalled clients, protected-store DACLs, migration races, upgrade/restart behavior, and per-user versus per-machine uninstall cleanup therefore lack repeatable end-to-end coverage. Add an integration harness that provisions the signed package, drives accepted and denied clients under distinct tokens, validates data preservation and isolation, and runs the negative lifecycle cases before this security-sensitive change is merged.
